prompt: How many inscriptions have been found on Pompeii’s walls?
explanation: Archaeologists have recorded more than 11,000, left by all kinds of people, from shopkeepers to enslaved workers.

options.text: Only the candidates themselves, in charcoal

explanation: Election dipinti were carefully made by professional signwriters, like sponsored ads.

prompt: A graffito calls the gladiator Celadus the girls’ idol. How do historians read it?

options.text: Probably as a boast written by Celadus himself
As proof he was Rome’s most famous gladiator
As an official notice from the amphitheatre

explanation: Graffiti are personal opinions; historian Alison Cooley thinks Celadus most likely wrote it himself.
misconception: An ancient inscription isn’t a fact just because it’s old: its writer had their own motives.
